original_question: Let X be a smooth acyclic surface such that for every non-constant regular function p in C[X] there exists q in C[X] with F = (p, q) : X -> C^2 a proper morphism. Must X be isomorphic to C^2?
target_in_paper: Section 1 ("Acyclic Surfaces"), item 1.7, Question: "Let X be a smooth acyclic surface such that for any non-constant regular function p in C[X] there exists another one q in C[X] with the property that F=(p,q):X->C^2 is a proper morphism. Is it true that X is isomorphic to C^2?" ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the official problem almost verbatim: the object X, the universal quantifier over every non-constant p in C[X], the existence of q in C[X], the requirement that F=(p,q):X->C^2 be proper, and the conclusion asking whether X must be isomorphic to C^2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))
missing_details: State explicitly that X is in the complex affine algebraic category: a smooth complex affine algebraic surface. This is implicit from the use of C[X] and the target C^2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))

To make the question fully stand-alone, unpack 'acyclic'; standard usage is H_i(X;Z)=0 for all i>0, and the paper later identifies acyclic surfaces with complex homology planes. ([boletin.math.org.mx](https://boletin.math.org.mx/pdf/2/37/BSMM%282%29.37.115-138.pdf))
It is worth saying that the paper asks only for some q in C[X]; it does not separately impose any extra hypothesis on q beyond making F proper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))
Clarify that F=(p,q):X->C^2 is a proper algebraic morphism; elsewhere in the paper, for affine morphisms, 'proper' is glossed as 'finite'. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))

Specify that 'X is isomorphic to C^2' means algebraically isomorphic to the affine plane over C, not merely biholomorphic or diffeomorphic. This matters because nearby questions in the paper explicitly distinguish algebraic isomorphism from biholomorphism. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))

No extra assumptions such as contractibility, log-Kodaira dimension conditions, or Q-acyclicity belong in the final formulation; those appear only as nearby context and motivation, not in item 1.7 itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))
refined_question: Let X be a smooth complex affine algebraic surface with H_i(X;Z)=0 for all i>0 (i.e. an acyclic surface, equivalently a complex homology plane). Assume that for every non-constant regular function p in C[X] there exists a regular function q in C[X] such that the algebraic morphism F=(p,q):X->C^2 is proper. Must X be algebraically isomorphic to the affine plane C^2? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 1, item 1.7 rather than the neighboring rigidity questions: the wording and quantifiers match item 1.7 essentially exactly. The surrounding text gives the intended scope and motivation: on C^2 every non-constant polynomial p can be completed by some q to a proper map (p,q), whereas for a contractible surface of log-Kodaira dimension 1 with its distinguished curve l_X=p^*(0), no such q exists for that p. So the paper's intent is a sharp characterization problem for the affine plane among smooth acyclic surfaces, not a broader question about all contractible or Q-acyclic surfaces. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))
